issues.revision: fully assignable at any time prior to closingClosing to Optionee's developer

judgments.title: Nominal Option Consideration
judgments.reason: The stated consideration is unambiguous. Its adequacy relative to the Option’s value and Optionor’s expenses is a bargaining concern.

judgments.title: Utility Representation Limited to "Current Use" Only
judgments.reason: “For its current use” clearly limits the utility representation. Its commercial inadequacy for the contemplated development is not a construction defect.

judgments.title: Utility Representation Limited to "Current Use"
judgments.reason: The utility representation expressly concerns the Property’s current use and does not promise adequacy for future development. The proposed clarification would reinforce an already apparent limitation.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: Property
judgments.reason: In context, lowercase “property” plainly refers to the Property that is the subject of the agreement. Capitalization inconsistency does not create a different reasonable referent.

judgments.title: Environmental Representation Qualified by "Actual Knowledge" — No Duty to Investigate
judgments.reason: “Actual knowledge” is a recognizable limitation and clearly excludes a broader inquiry-based standard. The issue seeks a more favorable warranty rather than construction of uncertain text.

judgments.title: Inconsistent section reference terminology
judgments.reason: “Paragraph 7(d)” unmistakably points to the identified subsection despite the document’s occasional use of “Section.” The terminology difference does not create referential uncertainty.

judgments.title: No Indemnification for Breach of Environmental Representations
judgments.reason: This concerns an omitted indemnity, not ambiguity or inconsistency in the representations that were included.

judgments.title: Representations Survive Indefinitely Through Option Exercise
judgments.reason: The bring-down obligation is clearly stated to continue through exercise. A materiality qualifier would soften the obligation rather than clarify uncertain language.

judgments.title: Representations Should Survive Closing
judgments.reason: The representations are expressly brought down through exercise of the Option. Whether they should survive longer is a negotiation issue.

judgments.title: "Best Efforts" Obligation for TIF Reimbursement is Overreaching
judgments.reason: “Best efforts” is a context-dependent performance standard whose required level of effort can have uncertain boundaries and require judicial construction.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Brownfield Plan
judgments.reason: “Brownfield Plan” is used in connection with Michigan Act 381 and governmental approval, giving it an externally ascertainable statutory context. Lack of a standalone definitions section does not by itself make the term ambiguous.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Brownfield Plan
judgments.reason: The term is tied to Michigan’s statutory Brownfield framework and governmental approval process, making its subject ascertainable. Merely lacking a formal definition does not establish lexical ambiguity.

neg17.clause_name: 8. Limitation of Liability for Unapproved Due Care Costs
neg17.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Optionor's Environmental Liability Cap May Be Insufficient
judgments.reason: The $500,000 cap is definite. Whether that amount adequately protects against environmental costs is a commercial allocation issue.

judgments.title: Optionor Bears Due Care Costs Up to $500K
judgments.reason: The $500,000 Due Care allocation is clear. Requiring consultation or an appeal process would add procedural protections rather than cure ambiguity.

judgments.title: Closing Date Lacks Extension Mechanism for Delays
judgments.reason: The 90-day closing deadline is clear, and the requested extension mechanism is an omitted commercial protection.

judgments.title: "As Is" Conveyance May Undermine Environmental Protections
judgments.reason: The issue concerns the potential tension between Section 10’s “as is” conveyance and Section 7’s representations and environmental obligations. The broad exception for matters “otherwise provided” likely harmonizes them, but the asserted construction question arises from those provisions’ relationship.

judgments.title: No Minimum Interest on Outstanding Balance
judgments.reason: The clause clearly permits interest only to the extent the City or State pays interest to the Developer, including the possibility of zero interest. A minimum rate would change the bargain rather than clarify it.

judgments.title: "As Is" Conveyance Weakened by Broad Optionor Representations
judgments.reason: The asserted issue arises from the relationship between Section 10’s “as is” language and Section 7’s affirmative representations. Although “except as otherwise provided” likely preserves Section 7, construing their interaction presents the claimed tension.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: Closing
judgments.reason: Lowercase “closing” plainly refers to the transaction’s closing event. The capitalization inconsistency does not create a genuine alternative meaning.

neg20.clause_name: 11. Optionee's Right to Enter and Inspect the Property
neg20.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Vague Notice Requirement for Property Entry
judgments.reason: “Reasonable notice” is a context-dependent standard with no specified minimum period, leaving its temporal boundary for entry uncertain.

judgments.title: Typographic error marker found
judgments.reason: The underscores are a harmless formatting artifact following the section number and do not affect the heading’s or provision’s meaning.

judgments.title: Survey Deadline Is a Fixed Date That Has Already Passed
judgments.reason: December 31, 2006 was a future deadline when this August 2006 agreement was executed. Its being historical now does not create an intrinsic construction defect in the original contract.

judgments.title: Optionee's Unilateral Termination Right Over Cost Allocation
judgments.reason: The unilateral termination right is explicit. Its lack of reciprocity may be unfavorable but is not ambiguous or internally inconsistent.

judgments.title: "Best Efforts" Reimbursement for Traffic Studies is Non-Binding
judgments.reason: “Best efforts to secure funds” leaves the extent of the required efforts uncertain, especially where funding depends on federal appropriations, even though it does not guarantee reimbursement.

judgments.title: Weak Reimbursement Obligation for Traffic Study Costs
judgments.reason: “Best efforts to secure funds” is an indefinite efforts standard whose required conduct is uncertain; it is not equivalent to a firm reimbursement promise.

judgments.title: No Optionor Termination Right for Non-Exercise
judgments.reason: Section 14 clearly provides termination without further obligation upon non-exercise. Reimbursement of Optionor’s expenses would add a new substantive obligation.

judgments.title: Brownfield Plan Approval Deadline Predates Option Expiration Without Consequence
judgments.reason: The issue seeks an express remedy for missing the approval deadline. The omission of that remedy is not itself ambiguity or internal inconsistency.

judgments.title: Brownfield Plan Approval Deadline Solely on Optionor
judgments.reason: The clause assigns Optionor responsibility for obtaining approval and permits specified extensions. Whether that obligation should instead be limited to reasonable efforts is a risk-allocation question.

neg28.clause_name: 12. Retention of Outstanding Balance Pending Approval
neg28.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Outstanding Balance Held Indefinitely if Brownfield Not Approved
judgments.reason: “Until such time as” approval is obtained clearly creates an approval-contingent retention period, even if it can last indefinitely. An outside date or escrow mechanism would be an added commercial protection.

judgments.title: Typo: "it" Should Be "its" in Assignment Section
judgments.reason: “In it sole discretion” contains a grammatical error; the possessive “its” is required for the phrase to operate as intended.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Contracting Officer
judgments.reason: Section 19 expressly identifies Mr. Forrest Hudson as the Contracting Officer for this Option. No additional definition is needed to determine the referenced person or role.

judgments.title: No Cap on Timeline for Outstanding Balance Payments
judgments.reason: The payment obligation may continue indefinitely, but the provision clearly ties payments to TIF reimbursements until the balance is paid. The absence of an outside date is a commercial risk, not a construction defect.

judgments.title: Deferred Balance Contingent on TIF Reimbursement
judgments.reason: The deferred balance is clearly contingent on receipt of TIF reimbursements, even though this may delay or prevent full payment. The requested outside date is a negotiated protection.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: tax incremental financing
judgments.reason: The lowercase and capitalized uses plainly describe the same TIF reimbursement mechanism in the same paragraph. Inconsistent capitalization alone does not affect construction.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "ferninine"
judgments.reason: “Ferninine” is an obvious misspelling of “feminine” and does not reasonably alter the provision’s meaning.

judgments.title: Grammar error: "portion I which"
judgments.reason: “Portion I which” is grammatically malformed because “in” has been mechanically replaced or truncated, impairing the sentence’s literal syntax.

judgments.title: Typographic marker in Section 15
judgments.reason: “Portion I which” is a mechanical grammatical error; replacing “I” with “in” restores the necessary prepositional phrase.

judgments.title: Spelling error
judgments.reason: The misspelling “ferninine” is transparently understood as “feminine” and does not change the provision’s meaning.

judgments.title: Outdated Contract Disputes Act Citation
judgments.reason: The citation was accurate when the agreement was executed, and the statute is unmistakably identified by name. Later recodification does not create a contractual ambiguity.

judgments.title: Disputes Subject to Federal Contract Disputes Act
judgments.reason: Application of the Contract Disputes Act and the resulting federal forum are clear risk allocations. The historical statutory citation does not obscure which Act applies.

judgments.title: Authority Provision References Wrong Entity Type
judgments.reason: The partnership-document requirement is expressly conditional on Optionor being a partnership, while the general resolution requirement can apply to the LLC. Tailoring the provision more specifically to an LLC would be prudent but is not necessary to construe the existing language.

judgments.title: Authority Provision References Partnership — Optionor is LLC
judgments.reason: The partnership language applies only “if” Optionor is a partnership, which it is not; the general resolution requirement remains applicable. LLC-specific documentation could be added, but the conditional language creates no operative contradiction.

judgments.title: Partnership Agreement Reference Should Be Operating Agreement
judgments.reason: The partnership-agreement requirement is part of a conditional branch applicable only if Optionor is a partnership. Because Optionor is an LLC, adding an operating-agreement reference would improve tailoring rather than cure ambiguity.

judgments.title: No Optionor Covenant Against Encumbrance During Option Term
judgments.reason: This identifies an omitted protective covenant, not ambiguity, mechanical error, or inconsistency in the existing text.

judgments.title: Conveyance Standard Unreasonably High — "Indefeasible" Title
judgments.reason: “Indefeasible” imposes a stringent title standard but has an ascertainable legal meaning, and the sentence expressly qualifies the no-encumbrance requirement by the Permitted Exceptions. The objection principally concerns commercial severity.

judgments.title: No Consequence for Optionor's Failure to Deliver Marketable Title at Closing
judgments.reason: The issue concerns the absence of an additional remedy. It does not identify ambiguous wording or a conflict among existing provisions.

judgments.title: Survey Costs Entirely on Optionor
judgments.reason: The contract clearly places survey costs on Optionor and permits Optionee to select Table A items. The lack of a cost cap is a commercial burden, not a construction issue.

judgments.title: Inconsistent Party References in Title Insurance Section
judgments.reason: The unexplained switch from the defined parties “Optionor” and “Optionee” to “Seller” and “Purchaser” is a boilerplate drafting error that leaves the literal party references undefined.

judgments.title: Undefined "Purchaser" Reference
judgments.reason: “Purchaser” is an undefined substitute for the defined term “Optionee,” reflecting a mechanical failure to conform the boilerplate terminology.

judgments.title: Assignment Without Optionor Consent
judgments.reason: The agreement clearly permits assignment without Optionor’s consent and gives Optionee sole discretion to evaluate the Developer. Additional disclosure rights are a negotiation matter.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Seller
judgments.reason: “Seller” is an undefined boilerplate substitution for the agreement’s defined “Optionor,” creating a literal party-reference error.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Purchaser
judgments.reason: “Purchaser” is an undefined boilerplate substitution for “Optionee,” resulting from failure to conform the title-insurance language to the defined party terminology.

judgments.title: No Right to Terminate for Uncurable Title Defects
judgments.reason: The provision expressly lists the available title-defect responses. The absence of a fourth option permitting termination is a remedy-allocation issue, not textual ambiguity.

judgments.title: Optionee Can Deduct Title Cure Costs Without Optionor Cure Period
judgments.reason: The premise is contradicted by Section 6 itself, which gives Optionor 21 days after notice to cure before the listed remedies apply. No construction defect is identified.

pos1.clause_name: Paragraph 2 — Term of Option (exercise by written notice)
pos1.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: Limited Extension Period Insufficient for Federal Procurement
judgments.reason: The single 30-day extension is clear; whether it is sufficient for procurement purposes is a negotiation concern.

judgments.title: Ambiguous Option Term — "Not Less Than" One Year
judgments.reason: “Not less than one year” supplies only a minimum duration while the clause relies on an unspecified “expiration.” This leaves the Option’s maximum term and expiration date uncertain.

judgments.title: No Governing Law Provision
judgments.reason: The absence of an express governing-law clause is an omission, not an intrinsic defect or contradiction between provisions.

judgments.title: Notices Provision Lacks Email/Electronic Notice Option
judgments.reason: The permitted notice methods are expressly and clearly enumerated. Adding email would modernize the clause but does not resolve a construction defect.
